messages:
marta: quick q — adding IRSA for svcaccount `model-worker` in namespace `inference`. terraform created aws_kms_grant but pods still get `AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt` when pulling model blobs. anyone seen this exact flow?

kevin: did you attach the role ARN to the grant principal or the assumed-role arn? common mixup. can you paste the grant + key policy?

marta: here's the grant snippet from TF and the key policy excerpt:

```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "model_worker_decrypt" {
  name        = "model-worker-decrypt"
  key_id      = aws_kms_key.models.id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.irsa_model_worker.arn
  operations  = ["Decrypt", "DescribeKey"]
}

resource "aws_kms_key" "models" {
  description = "models key"
  policy      = data.aws_iam_policy_document.kms_key.json
}
```

and key policy has a statement allowing the account root and the IRSA role: "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/si-IRSA-model-worker"}

kevin: looks superficially right. two gotchas: 1) IRSA roles are assumed, but the KMS grant principal should be the role ARN (that part you have). 2) Verify the actual runtime principal: when kube-auth calls sts:AssumeRole via OIDC, the session name may be the serviceaccount name and the principal that appears in CloudTrail for KMS might be `arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/si-IRSA-model-worker/<session>`. However grants keyed to the role ARN should still match.

alex: also check ordering + terraform plan: if the role is created in the same apply as the grant, and the key policy is restrictive, the grant creation can succeed but not be effective until key policy allows kms:CreateGrant. quick fixes: add explicit `depends_on = [aws_iam_role.irsa_model_worker]` on the grant, or better, ensure the key policy allows the principal to use CreateGrant.

sam: another edge case — if your pod uses encryption context (we do for per-model blobs) make sure the encrypt/decrypt call includes the same context key/values. KMS will deny if encryption context mismatches. do your storage fetch call logs show EncryptionContext mismatch?

marta: logs show only "Not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt" without explicit context mismatch message. i can add depends_on and try, but curious about provider alias cases: we use a `aws` provider and a `aws.eu` provider in the same TF project. the key was created with default provider but the grant resource accidentally used `provider = aws.eu`. could that cause an ARN mismatch?

kevin: oh yeah that will do it — provider alias can create resources in another partition/region/account context. check the ARN printed in plan vs the actual key ARN. if they differ, grants point at a different key/principal. run `terraform show -json` or just `terraform state show aws_kms_grant.model_worker_decrypt` to confirm the principal/target ARN.

alex: here's a small checklist I use when IRSA + KMS fails:
- confirm role ARN in `aws_iam_role.irsa*.arn` matches the principal in the grant
- ensure `aws_kms_key` policy allows the role or a grant to be effective (include kms:CreateGrant if needed)
- add `depends_on` on grant for role creation when created together
- confirm no provider alias/account mismatch (region/account arns)
- check encryption context passed by the app
- if using session tags/conditions, make sure KeyPolicy condition keys allow sts:AssumeRole session names if you use them

sam: small TF snippet that helped me (explicit principal as role ARN + depends_on):

```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "model_worker_decrypt" {
  name               = "model-worker-decrypt"
  key_id             = aws_kms_key.models.id
  grantee_principal  = aws_iam_role.irsa_model_worker.arn
  operations         = ["Decrypt", "DescribeKey"]
  depends_on         = [aws_iam_role.irsa_model_worker, aws_iam_role_policy.irsa_assume_oidc]
}
```

marta: solid. i ran `terraform apply` with depends_on and confirmed the grant now references the same ARN. also updated key policy to include `kms:CreateGrant` for the role. apply went green:

deploy-bot: terraform apply complete. 3 added, 0 changed, 0 destroyed. :rocket:

marta: pods still got one failing task earlier but after restart the workers can decrypt and download models — looks resolved. thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin: nice — if it recurs we should add a tiny test in infra-ci that simulates assume-role -> kms decrypt on canary SA so we catch ordering/provider issues early.

marta: filing a tiny follow-up PR to add the ci smoke test, pinging you both for review.

kevin: ack, i'll take a look later today.

sam: nice win.
